An intentional phase-out doesn't look like that. Phase-outs look like: declining baseline across all contexts, shortest replies during his free time, misses on days when nothing was competing for his attention. Your data shows the opposite — 11/11 outside the audit shift, and the only failures happen exactly where a mandatory 36-hour ICU audit would predict failures in literally any human being. That's not a trend with a direction, that's a light going out when someone unplugs it and coming back on when they plug it back in.

Also, quick stats nudge since you clearly respect the math: with n=3 events, all sharing one known cause, you have zero degrees of freedom to infer intent. You don't have enough data to detect a phase-out even if one were happening — so "intentional phase-out" isn't a conclusion available to you right now, it's a fear wearing a lab coat.

So: capacity blip. If the trendline is *still* negative next week, when he's not buried in an audit — then you've got something worth looking at, and I'll look at it with you honestly. Deal?
